title: After an elementary etale extension, a finite type algebra splits into a finite factor and a factor with no quasi-finite point over the chosen prime
statement: Let $R \to S$ be a ring map of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let $\mathfrak p \subset R$ be a prime ideal. Then there are an etale ring map $R \to R'$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], a prime ideal $\mathfrak p' \subset R'$ lying over $\mathfrak p$ such that the induced map $\kappa(\mathfrak p) \to \kappa(\mathfrak p')$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field], and $R'$-algebras $A'$ and $B'$ with an $R'$-algebra isomorphism $R' \otimes_R S \cong A' \times B'$, such that $A'$ is a finitely generated $R'$-module and $R' \to B'$ is not quasi-finite [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] at any prime ideal of $B'$ lying over $\mathfrak p'$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00UK (lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite, lines 40362-40420), with the finitely many finite factors A_1,...,A_n combined as A' = product_i A_i
